answer: Time-locked referral chains. Each new identity must be introduced by an existing member who co-signs its first transactions, and that co-signature only matures after a fixed delay during which the introducer cannot wander to a fresh account without losing standing. The introducer's slot becomes a scarce haven tied to real activity history, so an attacker must either wait out every delay per identity or buy aged accounts from members who rarely exist. Sable margins of fake identities collapse because each one costs an introducer's irreplaceable tenure, not money.
